title: A language switch empties settled Swatch matches and disables Share
evidence: The locale subscriber calls inherited update(), which renders a fresh matchResultsContainer and a fresh disabled share button. renderRightPanel ends by updating selection card, empty state, grid and handoff only. updateColorGrid never calls updateMatchResults or updateShareButton, and Swatch has no onUpdate override. selectedColor and matchedDyes survive but their cards do not. A pending price completion can accidentally repopulate cards, so use a settled selection with prices off.
repro: Pick a swatch cell with market prices off and observe match cards plus enabled Share. Switch language. The selected cell/selection sentence remain, but cards are gone and Share is disabled. Pick a cell again to restore them.
test_gap: swatch-tool.test.ts:1162-1169 rerenders only a loaded character card; :1324-1335 checks slot naming; :2027-2035 checks listener cleanup after update. None asserts forward matches and share state survive update. No suite was run by this reviewer.
fix: Restore the derived match cards and share parameters during/after every render without reloading the selected cell or duplicating subscriptions; add a settled forward-match locale regression.
overlap: Oct4 BUG-021 covered Harmony/Mixer/Comparison/Accessibility; this is the same failure class in Swatch, absent from that finding scope. Those four have restorative onUpdate paths today.

title: A completed preset edit can dismiss a different modal
evidence: showPresetEditForm discards the ID returned by ModalService.show. The form remains closable and Cancel remains enabled while editPreset/upload/remove awaits. Success then calls dismissTop(), so cancellation followed by another modal causes the old completion to dismiss that unrelated top modal.
repro: Start a valid edit against a delayed response. Cancel the edit, open another modal, then resolve editPreset successfully. The newly opened modal is dismissed by the original edit completion.
test_gap: preset-edit-form.test.ts:268-289 uses a deferred edit but checks only busy/restored button labels; it never closes the form and opens another modal before resolving. No suite was run.
fix: Keep the edit form modal ID and dismiss only that ID, mirroring the submission form. Keep the callback semantics explicit when the initiating modal has already closed.
overlap: Oct4 BUG-102 was the submission form and is fixed there using state.modalId. This independently surviving edit-form call is not that fixed source path.

title: Accessibility ignores saved canonical display options until a setting changes
evidence: Accessibility initializes cardDisplayOptions from DEFAULT_DISPLAY_OPTIONS and never reads getConfig(accessibility). Its subscription only handles future broadcasts; ConfigController.subscribe merely registers a listener and does not replay current state. The sidebar loads current canonical options, so persisted showHex=false/showRgb=false/showCmyk=true disagree with cards after entering/reloading the tool. Legacy vision-type restoration does not restore these card options.
repro: Change global color-format options on another tool (for example hide HEX, enable CMYK), then enter Accessibility or reload on it and select a dye. Sidebar switches show saved settings, but cards use default HEX/CMYK visibility until another display toggle broadcasts.
test_gap: accessibility-tool.test.ts:772-787 validates merging an explicit post-mount setConfig call. It does not preseed ConfigController, mount, and inspect first-render card properties.
fix: Seed Accessibility display options from ConfigController before the first results render, then subscribe to changes. Retain intentional tool-specific metadata restrictions.
overlap: Oct4 BUG-022 fixed first-render dye filters in four other tools; it did not cover Accessibility display options.

title: Harmony ignores canonical harmony type on initialization and reset/import broadcasts
evidence: The constructor restores selectedHarmonyType and companionDyesCount from legacy keys. onMount reads canonical harmony config but omits both of those fields. The controller subscription updates companions but never selectedHarmonyType. Direct sidebar type edits appear to work because the separate config-change bridge calls setConfig; resetAllConfigs/importConfigs broadcast without that bridge. Sidebar/serialized settings then say complementary (or imported type), while tool rail, wheel and results retain the legacy/current type.
repro: Choose Triadic, open Advanced Settings and reset settings; return to Harmony results. The canonical/sidebar type is Complementary, but the results/rail remain Triadic. A fresh mount after importing a different type similarly reads the old legacy type. Companion count may initially disagree until a future harmony broadcast.
test_gap: harmony-tool.test.ts:999-1029 tests direct tool.setConfig(type) and legacy writes; later controller regressions exercise wheel/market. They do not reset/import canonical type and compare sidebar, rail and output.
fix: Use the canonical harmony config as the initial authority for type/count, and apply harmonyType through the controller subscription with the existing pin-clearing and regeneration behavior. Avoid redundant full regenerations from the bridge.
overlap: Old sidebar controller mirroring BUG-027 is fixed in ConfigSidebar.mirror; the remaining tool-side omission is distinct.

title: Comparison ignores the global Stain and Spectrum display switches
evidence: Comparison setConfig applies the five color formats, delta and price only. It never assigns showStain or showSpectrum. Both card render paths read optional fields with ?? true, so those rows remain enabled despite the visible global switches and canonical config becoming false. An exact-source method extraction confirmed setConfig({displayOptions:{showHue:false,showStain:false,showSpectrum:false}}) leaves all three current properties true.
repro: On Comparison select one or two dyes. Turn off Stain and Spectrum in Options. Both switches remain off, but cards still show the stain readout and spectrum row. Navigate away/back: those fields are still default-on in the tool.
test_gap: comparison-tool.test.ts:425-443 merely calls setConfig and asserts leftPanel has children. It does not inspect rendered card properties or rows, and its fixture omits the new options.
fix: Apply the complete supported DisplayOptionsConfig key set, preferably through the shared helper. Seed it from canonical settings and test the single-card and duel-card rows.
overlap: Related to the incomplete display-key class of Oct4 BUG-027/039, but current comparison setConfig still lacks these 5.0 fields. Acquisition/delta rows have deliberate comparison-specific comments and are not included in this claim.

title: Palette-driven Gradient and Comparison selections do not request their prices
evidence: Gradient updates interpolation for endpoint picks, pins and algorithm changes without fetching prices; its only calls to fetchPricesForDisplayedDyes are in market-config handlers at :637/:649. Comparison.addDye, used by selectDye from the live v4 drawer, updates cards/results/storage but never fetchAndUpdatePrices. Its old embedded-selector listeners do fetch, but the v4 palette route does not use them. With prices enabled before selection and cold cache, the displayed price rows stay empty until a market/display change triggers a fetch.
repro: Enable market prices, then select new Gradient endpoints or select Comparison dyes from the app-wide drawer while cache is cold. Observe no new price request and blank rows. Changing server/toggling prices causes them to load. Gradient restored selections have the same omission.
test_gap: gradient-tool.test.ts:1266-1275 proves server changes refetch after a ramp is mounted, not the ramp-selection trigger. comparison tests selectDye for selection logic and price tests exercise legacy MarketBoard relays, not a cold-cache v4 selection.
fix: Have the canonical results/selection-change path fetch the newly displayed dyes when price display is enabled, respecting existing service request coalescing and price toggles; cover direct v4 selectDye plus restored Gradient endpoints.
overlap: Oct4 BUG-086 fixed the AND visibility gate; both toggles are on in this reproduction. Mixer mixing-field clicks at mixer-tool.ts:1408-1423 also rerank without their usual fetch, but that sibling is not required for this candidate.

title: Preset card keyboard handling hijacks its Save and Vote buttons
evidence: The focusable article handles every bubbling Enter/Space keydown, unconditionally prevents default and selects the preset. Its nested Save/Vote buttons stop click propagation only. A keyboard activation on either button reaches the article first; it opens details and cancels the button activation. An exact-handler JSDOM probe produced selectedDetail=1 and defaultPrevented=true for Enter dispatched on the child Save button.
repro: Tab to Save or Vote on a preset card and press Enter or Space. The detail opens instead of saving/voting. Mouse clicks stop propagation and work normally.
test_gap: preset-card.test.ts:214-243 checks face-button visibility/labels; no keydown coverage exists in the file. The probe exercised the actual extracted handler with DOM bubbling, not a full browser or suite.
fix: Handle article keyboard activation only when the article itself is the event target, or use a separate open-details button so nested controls retain native keyboard behavior.
overlap: Oct4 BUG-028 fixed the global dye picker keyboard path; this is the separate nested preset-card action path.

title: Arming an empty Gradient End slot still writes the picked dye into Start
evidence: Clicking the End endpoint arms slot 1 and selectDye forwards that slot to setEndpoint. For an empty selectedDyes array, setEndpoint ignores idx and stores [dye], which is Start. An exact-source method probe of setEndpoint(1,dye) returned [dye] with startDye populated and endDye null. The dense-model comment explicitly says always fills Start first, so the coordinator should reconcile that legacy model rule with the new armed-slot UI contract before filing.
repro: Clear Gradient, click its empty End card, then pick a dye in the palette. Start fills while End stays empty, despite End being armed.
test_gap: gradient-tool.test.ts:1509-1545 exercises slot replacement/swaps with a complete existing ramp, never End-first on an empty tool.
fix: Either represent a pending End endpoint independently so an armed pick goes into End, or prevent/clearly explain End arming until Start is selected. Preserve serialization and existing no-duplicate rules.
overlap: Oct4 BUG-094 handled result-card swaps when both ends exist; those guards now work. This is the empty-selection branch and is marked design-contract-sensitive.

title: Editing a preset refreshes the public pool but leaves Mine and its edit baseline stale
evidence: The edit-success callback invokes loadPresets only. Mine renders userSubmissions, and opening the edit form resolves its baseline from that same array. It is populated at connection/sign-in and refreshed after deletion or My submissions modal actions, but not after this direct detail edit. After successful edit, Mine can still show the previous title/dyes and reopening Edit uses the old values until another submissions refresh/reload.
repro: From Mine open an owned preset and edit its name or dyes successfully. Return to Mine: its card still uses the old data. Reopen its Edit form: it is initialized from stale userSubmissions. Contrast delete success, which explicitly refreshes both sources.
test_gap: preset-tool.test.ts covers Mine first loading at :1321-1350 and votes/history, but contains no edit-success refresh assertion. No suite was run.
fix: Refresh or update userSubmissions on successful edit in addition to the public pool, including pending moderation fields, and assert the next Mine card/edit baseline reflects the authoritative response.
overlap: No matching current security/dead-code item found; this is distinct from modal ownership wcomp-002.
